title: RTEC Title VI public participation and outreach workflow — January 2026 plan
purpose: Provide meaningful opportunities for the public, including low-income, minority, LEP and other traditionally underserved communities, to receive information and comment before relevant transportation/service decisions are implemented.
goals: Inclusion and diversity through proactive outreach.
Physical, geographic, temporal, linguistic and cultural accessibility.
Clear and relevant explanation of proposed fare/service decisions.
Flexible participation options that can change over time.
methods: Telephone feedback recorded and passed to management.
Meetings designed as appropriate for information sharing, questions, priority setting, consensus-building or public comment before service changes.
Accessible meeting facilities, preferably served by public transit; use varied locations when a series of meetings makes that appropriate.
Multilingual flyers through community organizations, especially organizations serving LEP populations.
Distribution through libraries and civic locations.
Other methods required by law or agreement.
language_access: Materials about proposed and actual service adjustments are to be provided in English and any other language meeting the plan's safe-harbor criteria.

The plan records outreach practices including Spanish brochures, Spanish website service information, public-hearing notices offering disability/LEP accommodation, Spanish telephone-message portions and bilingual service resources.
feedback_handling: Phone feedback is recorded and passed to RTEC management.
Comments collected through participation methods are responded to as appropriate.
Public input is to be considered before implementing relevant proposed service adjustments.
hearing_history_in_2026_plan: The plan points to a FY2021 public-hearing letter/advertisement.
It states no public hearing was held for FY2023, FY2024 or FY2025 because there were no changes.
controls: Public-meeting format should match the purpose of the engagement.
Meeting sites must satisfy accessibility requirements.
Language accessibility is integrated into outreach rather than handled only after a complaint.
Outreach evidence should be retained with the plan/grant record so later submissions can show actual participation efforts.
currentness_and_data_quality: Historical outreach examples in the 2026 plan are evidence of prior practice; they are not proof that every channel is still active today.
Individual bilingual employees mentioned in the source should not be promoted to generalized knowledge; use role/capability data and maintain any live roster separately.
Public-facing English and translated content should be versioned together because the website audit found locale/document drift.
automation_candidates: Public-outreach evidence log linking each service/fare change to notices, meetings, comments, accommodations, translations and management response.
Automatic checklist for accessible venue, language needs, notice channels and required hearing/coordination evidence.
Version-sync checks for multilingual web/printed notices.
Grant-package generator that can pull current public-participation evidence without duplicating old attachments.
